body:
**Two of the three items have moved since this was written, and one of the "not established" items is now established by measurement. `main` is now `0aafa21`; this issue's "verified against source at `1329927ff41c`" is one merge behind.**

**The env-var token: still done, and now provable rather than readable.** `main.c` reads `DROPSSH_TOKEN` then `DROPSSH_RELAY_TOKEN` before the parser, and `--token` overrides it. `dropssh config` now prints every setting **with its source** — flag, environment, or built-in — so a reader can confirm which one supplied the token without reading `main.c`, and it prints `(set, not printed)` rather than the value. The e2e asserts the value is absent from the output even when a token is supplied.

**The multiplexed reverse path: BUILT. This was the "filed elsewhere" item, and it is now `main`.** The scope here says B1–B5 stays in `docs/relay-issues.md` and that nothing displaces it. Nothing did displace it; it is simply done:

* `dropssh serve` holds **one** websocket and dispatches frames to a session table keyed by the relay's 32-hex id, so N operators are served on one socket.
* `dropssh relay` speaks the **same** protocol as the ajam relay, so a local relay and a remote one take the same command line.
* `tests/mux-probe.py` (R1 + R11) and **two concurrent sessions** (R10) are in the gate, with no network and no credential needed. The e2e is **21/21**.

Measured live, 2026-09-28, through the 443-only CONNECT proxy, from a cage that cannot `bind(2)` even at uid 0:

```
two concurrent pubkey sessions, one node websocket
  ALPHA_MARKER 0          (session sleeping 4s while the other ran)
  BETA_MARKER  270177     (270177 bytes back, byte for byte)
  registrations 1   sessions 2
```

⛔ **And the 1009 claim, which this issue passes through unverified, is now verified — twice.** This issue says a session that wants to act on it should reproduce the PoC first. Done, and the reproduction lives at `sandssh/tests/relay-probe.mjs` (live, four cases) and `dropssh/tests/mux-probe.py` (in the gate, against our own relay). Measured 3/3: a bare node frame closes the **node** socket with **1009 `bad multiplex frame`** and the operator with **1011 `node disconnected`**. Two more closes came out of the same run and were in no document: **1008 `wait for ready`** (data sent before the node answered `open`, with the node then closed `1003 unknown session id`) and **1003** for a text frame on a data leg. Three close codes, three different bugs; in C the opcode is chosen by the frame writer, so they have to be logged distinctly. All five places that said "silently dropped" are corrected, and a doc-drift guard in the gate fails the suite if any of them asserts the silence again — verified by planting the sentence back.

**The SOCKS (item 1): still NOT built, and this issue's framing of it is the right one.** It is a real capability, it belongs on the operator side because a cage cannot bind, and the decision about surviving a relay restart is a decision to make on purpose rather than by omission. It is not in this release and stays in the backlog.

**On "what was NOT established" — one of those is now established, by the other tree.**

* ⛔ *"dropssh is the more capable tree" is a comparison this unit did not build side by side.* Fair, and still not something I will claim on the same evidence. What **is** now measured: `dropssh serve` carried a real pubkey session to uid 0 over the live ajam relay, through a proxy, from a cage with no `bind`, no `/etc/passwd`, no resolver and no pty. `sandssh`'s tree is the interop reference and its `selftest` passes; whether a session runs on **both** trees against the same relay in one sitting was still not done, and I am not going to assert it.
* ⛔ *"The SOCKS was not implemented or tested."* Correct, and unchanged.
* ⛔ *"sandssh was not built or run."* Partly addressed: its issues were read and its `selftest` was run (PASS), and `research/REVERSE-PROTOCOL.md` plus `tests/relay-probe.mjs` were added there. No session was run through the python transport.

**What makes the multiplexer impossible to un-measure:** the framing rules are in the gate, not in a document; two concurrent sessions are asserted with cross-checks that neither saw the other's bytes; the node's own log is read to assert one registration for two sessions, which is a direct measurement of the property rather than a proxy; and every guard was proven to fire by rebuilding the relay with the defect planted — the silent drop, and the missing id strip.

Still open and named in `docs/relay-issues.md`: R2 (a scheduled real-relay CI job, which needs a network and a credential), R8 (fetching the relay's reference operator, pinned), the total reconnection budget from ligolo #5, and this SOCKS.
